chunks: And in the narration of Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, he said:
A child grows every year by four finger-widths, measured by his own finger.

key_terms.أَصَابِعَ: finger-widths as a unit of measure
key_terms.بِإِصْبَعِ: by a finger; measured using a finger
key_terms.حَمَّادِ: Ḥammād, the named transmitter in the report
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: his own, indicating the child’s own finger as the measure

ai.seo_question: How much does a child grow each year according to the narration of Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā?
ai.summary: This report states a rule of thumb about a child’s yearly physical growth, expressing it in terms of finger-widths measured according to the child’s own finger. It appears in the context of evaluating and testing a child, indicating a practical observational standard.
